research_question: What is the effect of active treatment compared with sham on PTSD symptom severity change from baseline to post-treatment in intention-to-treat analyses with missing data imputation?
outcome_description: PTSD symptom severity change from baseline to immediately post-treatment assessed by a validated clinician-administered or self-report scale (intention-to-treat with imputation)
positive_direction: Greater reduction in PTSD symptom severity in the active treatment group compared to sham control (favoring active treatment)
search_queries: active sham PTSD symptom severity controlled trial
active versus sham posttraumatic stress disorder trial outcome
PTSD active sham experiment quantitative effect
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical trials comparing an active intervention to a sham control condition in individuals with PTSD
Assessment of PTSD symptom severity from baseline to post-treatment using a validated scale (e.g., CAPS, PCL)
Quantitative data reported or derivable for intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis with missing value imputation
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an active treatment and a sham control condition
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for PTSD symptom severity (e.g., missing means, SDs, test statistics, or model estimates)
Completely unrelated to PTSD or sham-controlled intervention research
moderators_to_extract: Intervention modality (e.g., rTMS, tDCS, stellate ganglion block, neurofeedback)
Imputation/ITT analytic method (e.g., mixed-model repeated measures, multiple imputation, baseline-observation-carried-forward)
PTSD outcome assessment instrument (e.g., CAPS-5, PCL-5)
Number of treatment sessions / intervention duration
effect_size_note: Intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis of change in PTSD symptom severity from baseline to post-treatment with missing data handled via imputation or mixed models, rather than per-protocol/completer analysis.
